entries.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
entries.reason: Own drawn frames: the family-15 incline body laid prone on the same pad (the instructions say chest-down; the stored template reads lying on the back and the instructions win - open question recorded at the checkpoint), legs to the floor. Full notes and open questions in the daily review.
entries.summary: Six drawn positions of a chest-supported dumbbell row on an incline bench.

frames.caption: Let both dumbbells hang from the shoulders with the chest on the pad.
Pull with the elbows toward the ceiling.
Row until the shoulder blades pinch.
Hold with the shoulder blades pinched.
Reach a full hang and let the blades stretch apart.

entries.name: Renegade Row
entries.reason: Source-bound draft, drawn from a 3D model turned 28 degrees so both floor dumbbells under the shoulders, the wide foot stance, the straight braced plank line, and the alternating row of each dumbbell to the waist without hip twist all read clearly: starting in a push-up plank on two dumbbells with wide feet, rowing one dumbbell to the waist while the supporting arm stays straight and the hips stay square, returning it to the floor, and rowing the other side.
entries.summary: In a push-up position with your hands on two floor dumbbells and your feet set wide, brace your abs and glutes to row one dumbbell to the side of your waist while keeping your hips square, lower it to the floor, then row the other side.

frames.caption: Set two dumbbells on the floor about shoulder-width apart and get into a push-up position with your hands on the handles and your feet wide for stability.
Brace your abs and glutes, and row one dumbbell up to the side of your waist while keeping your hips square to the floor.
Lower the dumbbell back to the floor under control while pushing the floor away through the supporting hand.
Row the other dumbbell up to the side of your waist without twisting the hips.
Lower the second dumbbell back to the floor under control to return to the braced plank.
